tx_indian_head_2.blurb: Indian Head is a river bluff in Hamm Creek Park, forming part of the Carrion Wall cliff line and easy to spot from the bank below. A dozen sport lines run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk sitting at 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers who already lead the middle grades. The lower sections of the wall are loose and crumbly, then the rock firms up as you gain height. Anchors are bolts only, with no lowering hardware, so bring gear and be ready to set up and clean from above. Expect a real hike in, along the shoreline or a trail, with plenty of thorny vines.

tx_landfill_wall.blurb: Landfill Wall is a limestone sport wall at Reimers Ranch in the Austin area, among the first sectors you meet on the south side of the creek. Twelve bolted routes run from 5.9 to 5.12, with most in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it is a better fit for intermediate and stronger leaders than for beginners. It sees fewer ascents than its neighbors and parts of it are a little overgrown, but the wall holds shade and the lines are worthwhile. One easy-looking climb near the left side starts up a big blobby tufa and heads for a roof.

tx_news_wall.blurb: News Wall is a compact granite wall on the backside of the Main Dome at Enchanted Rock, the smallest of the walls back there and the quickest to reach. Most of its twelve routes are short, under half a rope length, and mostly traditional, with a couple of bolted lines and a couple of top-rope options. Grades run from 5.4 to 5.10, with plenty at 5.6 to 5.9, making it a friendly spot for newer trad climbers. Bring a rack, since most lines need gear, and the same walk links to the neighboring backside walls.

tx_kingdom_the.blurb: The Kingdom is a cluster of granite boulders on the Little Dome side of Enchanted Rock, in the Kingdom of Zilch, at the eastern end of the front-side blocs. Almost all of the twelve lines are boulder problems, plus a single trad route at 5.10. Most problems fall between VB and V3, with a few much harder ones from V6 to V8 for strong boulderers. The boulders are building-sized and sit above the campsites, a short uphill walk from the car. The sun hits in the morning and the afternoon brings shade, with many places to escape the heat.

tx_different_strokes_wall.blurb: Different Strokes Wall is a small bouldering wall on the Nolan River near Blum, the first one you reach from the road and only a short walk across the river. Twelve problems spread from V1 to V7, so there is a little of everything: a handful of easy to moderate lines, several V5 and V6 traverses and sit-start problems, and one V7 for the strongest. The stone is good with pleasant angles, though the topouts tend to be dirty. It makes an easy first stop before moving on to the other walls along the river.
